Cosine similarity drift detector for embeddings

Source: R/dfr_cosine.R
dfr_cosine.Rd

Monitors a stream of embeddings (for instance BERT sentence embeddings of the texts sent to an NLP model) with the custom Model Monitor of Nigenda et al. (2022): every observation is scored by its average cosine similarity with the baseline embeddings (cosine_score()), the scores are averaged over monitoring windows of window_size observations, and a drift is reported when the average falls below threshold. Since it monitors the distribution of the inputs, it is used for virtual concept drift.

Usage

dfr_cosine(
  target_feat = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  n_reference = 1000,
  window_size = 1,
  threshold = 0.5
)

Arguments

target_feat

Names of the columns holding the embedding. NULL (the default) uses every numeric column.

reference

Optional baseline embeddings (a matrix or data frame with the monitored columns), such as the embeddings of the training texts. When NULL, the first n_reference observations of the stream form the baseline.

n_reference

Size of the baseline taken from the stream when reference is NULL.

window_size

Number of observations whose scores are averaged before the comparison with threshold (the monitoring window, an hour of traffic in the paper). With 1, every observation is checked on its own, as the reference code does.

threshold

A window whose average score is below it is a drift (0.5 in the reference code).

Value

dfr_cosine object. After fit(), drifter_output holds the score of every observation (score) and the average of the window on its last observation (window_score).

Details

The windows do not overlap; the drift is reported on the last observation of the window. Observations with missing values or zero norm are skipped. reset_state() keeps a baseline given in reference and empties the window; a baseline taken from the stream is forgotten, and the next n_reference observations form a new one.

References

Nigenda, D., Karnin, Z., Zafar, M. B., Ramesha, R., Tan, A., Donini, M. and Kenthapadi, K. (2022). Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor: A system for real-time insights into deployed machine learning models. In Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, 3671-3681. doi:10.1145/3534678.3539145

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
set.seed(1)
baseline <- matrix(stats::rnorm(2000, mean = 2), ncol = 20)
# From row 21 half of the coordinates change sign.
flipped <- matrix(stats::rnorm(400, mean = 2), ncol = 20) %*% diag(rep(c(1, -1), each = 10))
stream <- as.data.frame(rbind(matrix(stats::rnorm(400, mean = 2), ncol = 20), flipped))
detector <- dfr_cosine(reference = baseline, window_size = 10, threshold = 0.5)
model <- fit(detector, stream)
model$drifter_output[!is.na(model$drifter_output$window_score), ]
#>          score  window_score
#> 10  0.78239783  0.8035939636
#> 20  0.65578924  0.7993399742
#> 30 -0.03978513 -0.0370861591
#> 40 -0.07524117  0.0001798928
